summary: Egon Wellesz studied at the University of Vienna (~1904–1908). He later held posts at the University of Vienna (~1913–1938) and as a lecturer at the University of Oxford (1943).

Eido Shimano studied under Kengan Goto, Keizan Shirozou, and Soen Nakagawa, at Ryutaku-ji and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He served as abbot at the Zen Studies Society and held posts at New York Zendo Shobo-ji and Dai Bosatsu Zendo Kongo-ji.

A scholar in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies, Eiichi Imoto studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1953). He later held academic posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (~1964–1995) and Momoyama Gakuin University (~1995–2005).

A philosopher and scholar, Eiichi Makino studied at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1903). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1938), Chuo University (~1907), Shiraume Gakuen Junior College (~1953–1968), Kyushu University, and Tohoku University.
Eiichi Otani, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, studied at Toyo University (~1987–1996). He serves as a professor and dean at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
Working in Indology and philosophy, Eiichi Yamaguchi was a graduate student at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990) and later served there as a research assistant (attested 1990–1991).
Active in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and religious studies, Eiju Fukushima is attested as a faculty member at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society in 2026.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Eikan Taki has been a member of Taisho University and served as a lecturer at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute (attested 2006).
Eiki Hoshino, working in religious and Buddhist studies, studied at Taisho University (~1963–1967). He later served there as a professor in the Faculty of Humanities and as a director (~1980–2013).
A Buddhist studies scholar, Eiko Okukaze was a doctoral student at Bukkyo University (attested 2010) and is attested as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University in 2026.

An Indologist, Eileen M. Dimes earned her B.A. from the University of London by 1932. She worked in the library at SOAS University of London (1945) and served as Assistant Keeper for Modern Indian languages at the India Office Records (1959).

Historian Eileen Power was educated at Girton College, Cambridge, and the University of Paris. She later held academic appointments at the London School of Economics (~1921–1940) and the University of London (~1931–1940).

Eilhard Mitscherlich studied at Heidelberg, Paris (under Chézy and Silvestre de Sacy), Göttingen, Berlin, and Stockholm. He held posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1822) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1821–1863).

A scholar of Indology and linguistics, Eino Wälikangas earned his M.A. at the University of Helsinki (~1908–1914) under doctoral supervisor J. N. Reuter. He later taught Sanskrit at the University of Helsinki (~1915–1920).

Buddhist studies researcher Eisaku Okada studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014) and held posts at the JSPS (attested 2014), Kyoto University (attested 2015), and Koyasan University (attested 2014, 2026).
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Eisei Kojima is attested in 1976 as a professor at Ryukoku University and as president of Doho University.

Eishu Miyazaki, working in Buddhist studies and Japanology, studied under Gyoo Kageyama and at Rissho University (~1934–1937). He later held posts at Rissho University (~1949–1984) and Minobusan University.
A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Eishun Fushimi studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.
An Indologist and linguist who studied under Nils Simonsson, Eivind Kahrs has held a post at Queens' College (attested 2010) and serves as a Council member of the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).
Eiyin Yasuda, active in Buddhist studies, studied as a disciple under Gyōin Hashimoto around 1950 and completed his studies at Ryukoku University (~1957–1961).
